A1-01.scene: A late-night laboratory. A first meeting.
A1-01.heading: Asking where someone is from
A1-01.note: Tina calls Frank's stitches cool rather than frightening. Their first meeting gently overturns expectations, just as their friendship will.
explanations: “Exactly” adds emphasis to the detail you want to know.
A short, enthusiastic reaction can show surprise and approval.
Follow “I'm” with your name to introduce yourself.

A1-02.scene: At a café, looking at the menu.
A1-02.heading: Asking about a drink
A1-02.note: Green signals danger on Tina's planet, but becomes a favorite drink on Earth. Enjoy her big reactions and Frank's quiet replies.
explanations: Use “what's that” with a description to ask about something you notice.
Order with a quantity, an item, and “please.”
Use “favorite” to describe something you like best.

A1-03.scene: A busy school cafeteria at lunchtime.
A1-03.heading: Ordering at the cafeteria
A1-03.note: Tina seems weak until the smell of food instantly revives her. Her hunger leads to short, useful ordering expressions.
explanations: “Need” and “now” make an urgent wish clear.
Use this expression when joining a queue at a busy shop or cafeteria.
“Let's” invites someone to act; “first” shows the order.

A1-04.scene: At school, talking about Frank's hometown.
A1-04.heading: Describing your hometown
A1-04.note: Frank's village is quiet enough to hear snow, while Tina's planet is bright and noisy. Their preferences reveal their homes.
explanations: Use “where is” to ask about a location.
Follow “far from” with the place used as a reference.
“A few” means a small number of countable things.

A1-05.scene: At school, Tina shows a family photo.
A1-05.heading: Introducing people in a photo
A1-05.note: Tina's question about a father makes Frank reconsider his relationship with the scientist. A family photo reveals their backgrounds.
explanations: A basic way to introduce someone in a photo.
This can reassure someone who has apologized.
Use “like” before a noun to describe a similarity.

A1-06.scene: Monday morning, on the way to school.
A1-06.heading: Talking about Monday mornings
A1-06.note: Frank likes getting up early; Tina wants to sleep. Their very different Mondays send a familiar complaint in an unexpected direction.
explanations: A plural weekday refers to that day every week.
Ask what makes someone unhappy about something.
A friendly reply when someone wins a point in an argument.

A1-07.heading: Welcoming a friend to your room
A1-07.note: Among all the pink is a star chart that cannot be repainted. A favorite-color conversation reveals how Tina treasures home.
explanations: Use “welcome to” to greet someone arriving somewhere.
Describe a location farther along a corridor.
“But” connects two contrasting qualities in a short description.

A1-08.heading: Talking about how you travel to school
A1-08.note: Frank worries about the pink bicycle, so Tina points out how noticeable he already is. Even a ride invitation shows their different viewpoints.
explanations: Combine a way of traveling with a daily habit.
Learn “ride my bike” as a useful phrase.
Offer to take someone somewhere in a vehicle.

A1-09.scene: Outside in a park on a sunny day.
A1-09.heading: Inviting a friend to take a selfie
A1-09.note: Frank's face barely changes when asked to smile. Tina finds something to enjoy in that expression after all.
explanations: Use “take” when talking about taking a photo.
A short question can make a gentle request.
A brief instruction asking someone to look in a particular direction.

A1-10.heading: Talking about breakfast preferences
A1-10.note: Tina offers her own translation of Frank's restrained pancake review. The gap between his words and feelings shows their closeness.
explanations: “Usually” describes a normal habit.
Use “prefer” to say which option you like better.
A useful phrase when encouraging someone to try food.

A1-11.heading: Describing things in a classroom
A1-11.note: Tina mistakes the teacher's flowers for food. Pointing out objects turns into a small clash between Earth and her home planet.
explanations: “On” shows that something is on a surface.
Use “those are” to point to more than one thing.
Follow “please do not” with a verb to stop someone politely.

A1-12.scene: In a corner of the classroom.
A1-12.heading: Asking someone to take your photo
A1-12.note: One picture becomes forty as Tina fixes her hair and the light. Frank's phone cannot keep up with her search for perfection.
explanations: “Take a photo of” identifies who or what is photographed.
Here, “a second” means a short time.
“Full” means the phone has no storage space left.

A1-13.heading: Describing a teacher's personality
A1-13.note: Frank understands a teacher who never smiles. Tina's idea of a fun classroom differs from the classroom he finds comfortable.
explanations: Describe personality with “be” and an adjective.
“Mine” avoids repeating “my teacher.”
“A lot” shows that an action happens often.

A1-14.scene: After school, outside the school gate.
A1-14.heading: Making plans after school
A1-14.note: Invited to tennis, Frank plans to bring a book. His quiet interests meet Tina's wish for a lively supporter.
explanations: The present continuous can describe an arranged future plan.
Use “come watch” to invite someone to see an activity.
Follow “cheer for” with the person you support.

A1-15.heading: Asking what a friend is doing
A1-15.note: Even homework-focused Frank is a little interested in cat videos. Giving in to “just one” provides the final small joke.
explanations: A basic question about what someone is doing now.
A short follow-up question about duration.
Use “send” with a recipient and the thing to be sent.

A1-16.heading: Asking where to find a book
A1-16.note: Frank searches for science books while Tina heads for manga. Even her whisper is characteristically loud.
explanations: Use “look for” to say what you are trying to find.
A useful request when you need help.
Combine a general location with a direction.

A1-17.heading: Asking a price
A1-17.note: Tina accepts the apple price but divides the fruit her own way. Frank quietly challenges her delight in Earth mathematics.
explanations: Use “how much” to ask a price.
Order by giving the quantity and item.
Say this when handing someone an object or money.

A1-18.heading: Showing something you like
A1-18.note: Tina wants a smiling teddy bear to teach Frank. A cute discovery takes the conversation somewhere unexpected.
explanations: “So” makes the reaction stronger.
Use “look at” to direct attention to something.
Follow “it is hard to” with a verb to describe difficulty.

A1-19.heading: Buying stationery
A1-19.note: Frank only needs a pencil that writes; Tina cares about color and decoration too. The same item has different requirements for each.
explanations: Use “would like” to ask politely for an item.
A short shop assistant's question about additional purchases.
Say this when the amount or conditions are sufficient.

A1-20.heading: Sharing ice cream preferences
A1-20.note: Frank always chooses vanilla, until a taste of Tina's strawberry ice cream. He would apparently prefer to keep his new taste secret.
explanations: Use “do you like” to ask about preferences.
Make the thing you like the subject of your answer.
“Mine” stands for “my ice cream.”

A1-21.scene: At night, playing an online game together.
A1-21.heading: Reacting during a game
A1-21.note: Tina declares that tonight she will win. Learning how Frank spends his nights shakes her confidence. Short cries give the game its energy.
explanations: The past tense and “all week” describe preparation.
An informal expression of surprise or disbelief.
“Right” strengthens “now” to mean immediately.

A1-22.heading: Talking about hobbies
A1-22.note: Tina wants book-loving Frank to dance. The difference between moving and dancing becomes their small contest.
explanations: Follow “like to” with a verb to name a favorite activity.
“Too” means more than is helpful or wanted.
Use this while demonstrating how to do something.

A1-23.heading: Talking about weekend plans
A1-23.note: Movie aliens remind Tina of family. Her view from beyond Earth slips into even ordinary weekend plans.
explanations: Use “on” before a weekday.
“Will” describes a future action.
“Remind someone of” connects something with a memory.

A1-24.heading: Offering a snack
A1-24.note: Frank tries to stop the late-night snacks but gives in to one bite. The food disappears faster than their conversation.
explanations: Follow “want” with the thing you would like.
An informal question that leaves out “Do you.”
“All gone” means nothing is left.

A1-25.scene: Tina invites Frank to her birthday party.
A1-25.heading: Inviting someone to a birthday party
A1-25.note: The gift is secret, but Tina's favorite color is not. Frank's one-word answer reflects how well they know each other.
explanations: Use “come to” to invite someone to an event.
Use “on” for the day and “at” for the time.
Use this when keeping a gift or plan secret for now.

A1-26.heading: Lending a coat
A1-26.note: Frank hesitates between warmth and wearing pink. Tina thinks looking like a strawberry is another benefit.
explanations: Use “it is” to describe weather or temperature.
Here, “mine” replaces “my coat.”
“Put on” describes dressing; “it” goes between the two words.

A1-27.heading: Telling a bored friend a story
A1-27.note: The girl from the stars in Frank's story resembles Tina. Beginning and ending a story become a playful exchange.
explanations: “Bored” describes the feeling; stretching “so” adds emphasis.
Use “tell someone a story” when offering a tale.
Ask someone to continue talking or acting.

A1-28.heading: Describing symptoms and asking for help
A1-28.note: Tina worries about homework; Frank recommends rest. His agreement to visit comes with a reason that is very much his own.
explanations: “Have a cold” describes this illness.
Name the painful body part, then use “hurts.”
“Will you” asks whether someone will do something for you.

A1-29.heading: Explaining what you want at the hair salon
A1-29.note: Tina wants pink hair too. Frank's comment reveals that her supposedly secret love of pink is obvious to everyone.
explanations: “It” refers to hair; “shorter” asks for less length.
A concrete length makes your request clearer.
Use “make it” with a color to request a result.

A1-30.heading: Showing a friend something you bought
A1-30.note: Tina is proud of her half-price bargain. Asked to count her growing collection of pink belongings, she suddenly distances herself from Earth customs.
explanations: A phrase emphasizing that something is completely new.
Use “did” to ask about a past purchase.
“Percent off” describes a discount.

A1-31.heading: Asking directions and asking someone to repeat
A1-31.note: Tina hears the directions again but still confuses left and right. A short “Right” can both correct and confirm.
explanations: A basic way to ask where a destination is.
“Then” puts the directions in order.
A polite request when you did not catch what someone said.

A1-32.heading: Ordering a meal
A1-32.note: Tina's love of pink influences her food choices. She reinterprets tomato sauce to suit herself; Frank supplies the accurate color.
explanations: Combine an item and its size when ordering.
A short question from a server about drinks.
“Is fine” says that an option is acceptable.

A1-33.heading: Checking a familiar order
A1-33.note: Familiar drinks and their usual seats make repetition comforting rather than dull.
explanations: “Always” describes a habit; “at” locates the seat.
A short way to check an order or plan.
Reply to a negative statement by saying the other person is the same.

A1-34.heading: Inviting a friend to study by phone
A1-34.note: The café seats and drinks need no discussion. Tina explains her ability to anticipate Frank as an alien power.
explanations: “Free” asks about someone's availability.
“Do you want to” can ask a preference and make an invitation.
Add a time to “see you” when parting.

A1-35.heading: Encouraging a friend before a test
A1-35.note: Tina wants instant knowledge; Frank suggests one page at a time. Using a phrase from her planet, he offers to move slowly together.
explanations: “Ready” describes preparedness.
“At a time” expresses doing something in small steps.
“Let me help” offers your assistance.

A1-36.heading: Supporting a friend after a setback
A1-36.note: Tina fears telling her mother more than the result itself. Frank offers to sit beside her so she need not face the conversation alone.
explanations: A brief encouragement to make another attempt.
Use “tell” with a person and the information.
“Next to” means immediately beside someone.

A1-37.heading: Asking how to borrow a book
A1-37.note: Frank carefully finds one book; Tina finds twelve manga volumes. Even borrowing becomes a competition for her.
explanations: “Could” and “please” make a polite request.
A useful phrase while checking something for someone.
At a library, “check out” means borrow through the lending procedure.

A1-38.heading: Describing a lost item
A1-38.note: The little star on Tina's key is more than decoration. Collecting a lost object reveals her attachment to home.
explanations: “Lost” is the past tense of “lose.”
Ask about an object's appearance or features.
“Mine” identifies you as the owner.

A1-39.scene: Tina wants to share school gossip.
A1-39.heading: Talking about a rumor
A1-39.note: Frank ignores gossip until it concerns the two of them. He seems to agree they make an interesting pair.
explanations: A conversational opening to check whether someone knows the news.
“Well” describes how closely you know someone.
Ask for more detail about what others are saying.

A1-40.heading: Trying on clothes and asking for a size
A1-40.note: Three pink dresses gain another companion. Tina's perfect set does not match Frank's way of counting.
explanations: “Try on” means put on clothes to see whether they suit or fit.
“A small” refers to an item in a small size.
A standard expression when deciding to buy something.

A1-41.heading: Asking for advice about someone you like
A1-41.note: Frank approaches romantic advice by collecting answers. The gap between Tina's wish for sympathy and his logic drives the exchange.
explanations: “I think” makes a statement about feelings more tentative.
“Move on” means leave something behind emotionally and continue.
“Too” says that a quality is stronger than desired.

A1-42.heading: Applying for a job
A1-42.note: Tina is the applicant, but attention turns to sleepless Frank. His serious introduction sounds like a joke to the manager.
explanations: “Apply” expresses the wish to seek a job or similar opportunity.
A common question in a job application.
“A week” expresses an amount per week.

A1-43.heading: Introducing yourself to a new neighbor
A1-43.note: Hearing that the neighbor is a nurse, Tina mentions Frank's stitches. By the end, even the identity of the new resident seems reversed.
explanations: A greeting for a first meeting.
In this context, the question asks about someone's job.
Use “a” before a singular job noun.

A1-44.heading: Looking forward to a trip
A1-44.note: Tina's many photos start at a hundred. Trip planning reveals their personalities and her dedication to pictures.
explanations: “Want to see” describes something you hope to visit and view.
“Lots of” means a large number.
Add “more” to the number to describe days remaining.

A1-45.heading: Trying festival food
A1-45.note: The ingredient in takoyaki has a surprising profession on Tina's planet. Their cultural differences derail the conversation before the first bite.
explanations: Use “I see” to point out a discovery.
An invitation to try something, including unfamiliar food.
Ask about a dish's ingredients or contents.

A1-46.scene: On the sofa in Tina's room.
A1-46.heading: Watching a movie with a friend
A1-46.note: Both claim they are not scared, until the film begins. Frank even explains his fear as an attempt to help his friend.
explanations: Use “watch” for moving images such as films.
An informal way to agree with a negative statement.
“Hold” describes taking and supporting someone's hand.

A1-47.heading: Ordering coffee
A1-47.note: Frank needs no sugar or milk, but cannot omit his name too. A list of things he does not need creates a small misunderstanding.
explanations: A brief question offering two drink options.
Answer with your chosen option and “please.”
A common request for a name to identify an order.

A1-48.scene: At the post office near home.
A1-48.heading: Sending a parcel
A1-48.note: Frank sends a gift to Japan. Tina compares a week of delivery with her planet's speed, but Earth's pace is enough for him.
explanations: Use “send” with the object and destination.
Ask about the time needed for delivery or travel.
Check the amount you are about to pay.

A1-49.scene: In a karaoke room in their usual town.
A1-49.heading: Trying something difficult with a friend
A1-49.note: Tina treasures the song Frank did not want to sing. “I'm keeping it” suggests holding on to the memory of that moment.
explanations: “With me” invites someone to join an activity.
Ask someone to trust your knowledge on a particular point.
Use “choose” with the qualities you want.

A1-50.scene: At a Tokyo hotel reception at night.
A1-50.heading: Checking in at a hotel
A1-50.note: Frank values quiet more than a view. His polite room requests reveal preferences unlike those of an ordinary traveler.
explanations: A basic statement on arriving at a hotel or restaurant.
Use “could I have” to request something politely.
Use “far from” to check distance.

A1-51.heading: Asking the price and recipient of a gift
A1-51.note: Tina's souvenir is a present for Frank. His awkward response still shows how much he will treasure it.
explanations: A basic price question.
“Handmade” describes something made by hand.
“For” asks who will receive a gift.

A1-52.heading: Booking a medical appointment by phone
A1-52.note: The appointment concerns stitches on Frank's arm. Even an orderly booking conversation ends with Tina's love of pink.
explanations: “Make an appointment” means arrange a meeting or medical visit.
State that you want the earliest possible time.
“How about” introduces a specific suggestion.

A1-53.scene: A long conversation in a Tokyo hotel lounge.
A1-53.heading: Asking for a little more time
A1-53.note: Tina does not want the travel evening to end; Frank wants her to rest. Five extra minutes become three in a small negotiation.
explanations: “Not yet” means the time has not come.
Put “it” between “write” and “down” when asking someone to make a note.
“More” asks for extra time.

A1-54.scene: Trying to catch the next train.
A1-54.heading: Asking the time and platform
A1-54.note: With five minutes left, Tina gives Frank a new role for the day despite his no-running rule. Short directions create urgency.
explanations: Ask for the current time.
“Which” asks someone to select among several possibilities.
Short expressions for showing a direction and leading someone.

A1-55.scene: Buying train tickets for a trip.
A1-55.heading: Buying train tickets
A1-55.note: As Frank orders two return tickets, Tina checks their promise to travel together again.
explanations: Combine the number of tickets with a destination.
Check whether a ticket is one-way or return.
The present simple describes a scheduled departure.

A1-56.heading: Exchanging money at a bank
A1-56.note: Tina changes leftover yen but keeps a little as a souvenir. Amounts and forms make room for treasured travel memories.
explanations: “Exchange A for B” shows which currency you give and receive.
“Sign” means write your signature.
Say this when everything, including a procedure, is complete.

A1-57.heading: Confirming tomorrow's plans
A1-57.note: The same time and place are small promises Frank finds easy to keep, and values for that reason.
explanations: Add the next meeting time to “see you.”
A brief way to confirm a familiar arrangement.
Here, “keep” refers to keeping promises.

A1-58.scene: In a taxi in an unfamiliar city.
A1-58.heading: Giving a taxi driver a destination
A1-58.note: The busy city brings more than a quiet hometown to mind. A brief conversation reveals what Frank misses.
explanations: Use “take me to” to give your destination.
A casual question with words omitted.
This means feel comfortable or familiar, as if at home.

A1-59.scene: At the airport. Tina departs, checking documents and finding the gate.
A1-59.heading: Asking the way to an airport gate
A1-59.note: Walking time to the gate is also time left before parting. Tina's request to continue to gate four shows her reluctance to say goodbye.
explanations: A counter request for a travel document.
Say this when the necessary preparation is finished.
Add a way of traveling when asking how long a journey takes.

A1-60.scene: In front of the boarding gate.
A1-60.heading: Saying how you feel before parting
A1-60.note: A familiar farewell becomes a promise to stay connected across the stars. Frank answers goodbye in words that belong to their friendship.
explanations: Express sadness about being apart.
Here, “message” is used as a verb.
Promise to do something as frequently as possible.

A2-01.scene: An unexpected reunion in the street after several years.
A2-01.heading: Meeting an old friend again
A2-01.note: Years later, the coat and coffee preferences are unchanged. News of a lab interview recalls their first meeting.
explanations: Express surprise at an unexpected reunion.
“Hunting” can mean searching for somewhere to live.
A brief way to ask for someone's latest news.

A2-02.scene: Viewing an apartment with Tina, an agent, and Frank.
A2-02.heading: Checking an apartment's features
A2-02.note: Tina loves the idea of pink walls. Frank checks the warmth and rent, adding practical questions to her dream home.
explanations: Here, “free to” means allowed to, not without cost.
The passive describes changes made to the room.
Ask for a night to think before deciding.

A2-03.scene: A lazy afternoon together, discussing a popular show.
A2-03.heading: Sharing opinions about a TV show
A2-03.note: Frank likes the quietest scene but cried too. Claiming the tissues are for Tina reveals his embarrassment.
explanations: The present perfect asks about viewing experience.
Express being very absorbed in something.
“Make + person + verb” describes causing a reaction.

A2-04.scene: Practicing an interview the night before.
A2-04.heading: Practicing an interview introduction
A2-04.note: Frank's lab experience takes him back to the night he was created. Tina tries to keep his honesty while giving his story an interview-friendly order.
explanations: An interview prompt about your background and character.
Encourage someone to calm down.
An informal expression of confidence in a friend.

A2-05.scene: Outside a restaurant after an all-you-can-eat meal.
A2-05.heading: Talking about eating too much
A2-05.note: This time Tina checked whether the flowers were edible. She has learned something, though controlling how much she eats remains difficult.
explanations: “Too much” describes an excessive amount.
Here, a conversational way to suggest walking to ease the discomfort of overeating.
Informal “way” makes a comparative stronger.

A2-06.scene: Looking at the night sky and discussing home.
A2-06.heading: Comparing your hometown with your current city
A2-06.note: Even Tina's lively home planet has a quiet night sky. Different worlds leave both friends with a sky they miss.
explanations: Compare two places using a comparative and “than.”
“Sounds” gives an impression based on what you hear.
“Even” strengthens a comparison; “farther” describes distance.

A2-07.scene: At a car rental counter. Tina handles the booking, with Frank beside her.
A2-07.heading: Renting a car
A2-07.note: Tina's birthplace is Beyond the Stars. Frank calls it a small town, steering the paperwork back toward everyday reality.
explanations: “May I” makes a polite request to check something.
“Per day” asks for a daily rate.
“Before” shows what you want to do prior to deciding.

A2-08.heading: Talking about travel experiences
A2-08.note: Tina describes Hawaii's warmth in terms of its people. Frank's question reveals different meanings of the same adjective.
explanations: Use “have been to” with a number of visits to describe experience.
The present perfect asks about past experience up to now.
Introduce a reputation or opinion you have heard.

A2-09.scene: Tina phones a restaurant while Frank sits nearby.
A2-09.heading: Booking a restaurant by phone
A2-09.note: Tina enjoys the view but plans to use a four-person booking for two. She even counts Frank's appetite as another person.
explanations: “Book a table” means reserve a place at a restaurant.
A short question checking the number of guests.
Here, “take” asks whether a payment method is accepted.

A2-10.heading: Complimenting a new haircut
A2-10.note: Frank carefully cuts his own hair, so Tina appoints him her hairdresser. He negotiates a small task: just the bangs.
explanations: “Myself” emphasizes doing something without another person's help.
Ask how long a completed task took.
Here, “still” means without moving.

A2-11.scene: Looking back at last month's travel photos.
A2-11.heading: Remembering a trip through photos
A2-11.note: Temple and lake photos bring back travel moments and family calls. The picture Frank wants kept includes him too.
explanations: Describe giving or doing something in response to what you received.
This means immediately, as with the father's call here.
As a verb, “matter” means be important or make a difference.

A2-12.scene: The first day at the gym, with a trainer.
A2-12.heading: Asking how to approach gym practice
A2-12.note: Learning that rest days count as part of training suddenly motivates Tina. She hears the explanation through her love of resting.
explanations: A comparative explains what should take priority.
“Get sore” describes developing muscle pain.
“At least” specifies a minimum number.

A2-13.scene: Tina asks Frank about a message read but unanswered.
A2-13.heading: Talking about waiting for a reply
A2-13.note: Before Tina sends more messages, Frank suggests a break. Putting down the phone and walking gives her a concrete alternative.
explanations: A negative present perfect describes a situation continuing until now.
“Bother” means trouble or disturb someone.
“Instead” proposes a different action.

A2-14.scene: A cooking class where the instructor explains pasta.
A2-14.heading: Following cooking instructions
A2-14.note: The instructor stops Tina from adding a whole box of salt. Her impatience and appetite keep appearing between the cooking steps.
explanations: “Until” specifies the condition to reach before stopping.
“Drain” means remove water or liquid during cooking.
Use “taste” as a verb to ask to try a little food.

A2-15.scene: Tina tells Frank she managed to get tickets.
A2-15.heading: Inviting a friend to a concert
A2-15.note: After an hour securing tickets, Tina has planned the whole evening. Once Frank knows one is for him, he prepares for her singing too.
explanations: Get someone's attention before sharing exciting news.
“Sell out” means all tickets or products have been sold.
A short informal way to accept an invitation or plan.

A2-16.scene: At a hotel reception. Frank complains about noise.
A2-16.heading: Discussing noise at a hotel
A2-16.note: Frank may not sleep much, but still needs a quiet night. Details of his origins slip into his calm explanation, puzzling the receptionist.
explanations: “Next door” means in the neighboring room or home.
“Busy” can describe a phone line that cannot take a call.
A comparative requests an improvement in a condition.

A2-17.scene: Tina reports a group chat argument to Frank.
A2-17.heading: Discussing a group chat problem
A2-17.note: Frank thinks leaving after hurting someone does not make the problem disappear. They sort through events and decide whom to contact first.
explanations: Use “look” with an adjective to describe someone's apparent state.
Ask what triggered an argument or event.
“Apologize” is the verb for saying you are sorry.

A2-18.scene: Tina calls support because her email app is not working.
A2-18.heading: Explaining a computer problem
A2-18.note: Support can fix the email function. Whether the recipient of Tina's four-page message replies is another problem.
explanations: “Since” identifies when the problem began.
Ask whether someone has already tried a possible solution.
Use this when sharing an image of a technical problem.

A2-19.scene: Frank worries about Tina's repeated all-night study sessions.
A2-19.heading: Showing concern for a tired friend
A2-19.note: Frank tries to move Tina away from coffee, snacks, and her assignment toward rest. Offering to wake her answers her main worry.
explanations: The present perfect with “since” describes a continuing situation.
Here, “left” means remaining.
“Due” states a submission deadline.

A2-20.scene: At a book club, sharing opinions on the same novel.
A2-20.heading: Sharing thoughts about a novel
A2-20.note: A discussion of a character's arrival reminds Tina of their meeting. Frank's memory of their first words brings the story back.
explanations: “Think of” asks for an opinion or evaluation.
Describe an unexpected arrival.
“Remind + person + of” identifies an associated memory.

A2-21.scene: At a volunteer briefing. Frank is at reception.
A2-21.heading: Asking about volunteer work
A2-21.note: Frank checks carefully so he will not pull up the wrong plants. His thorough questions even change the estimated work time.
explanations: Use “need to” to ask about necessary preparations.
“What kind of” asks about the type of work.
“Pick up” means lift something from the ground.

A2-22.scene: Tina is at the mirror in her room before going out.
A2-22.heading: Asking about an outfit
A2-22.note: Tina sees a complete clothing disaster; Frank thinks a shoe change is enough. His own effortless clothing choices have a surprisingly simple explanation.
explanations: Informal “way” strengthens “too long.”
Use this for clothing or anything that does not fit its surroundings.
“Swap” means exchange one thing for another.

A2-23.scene: In the corridor of a building Frank has just moved into.
A2-23.heading: Asking a neighbor about building rules
A2-23.note: Frank already knows the rules better than a resident. A request for help becomes an offer to help.
explanations: “Move in” means begin living in a new home.
Ask where a shared facility is.
“Rinse out” means wash the inside of a container with water.

A2-24.scene: Tina rushes excitedly into a café.
A2-24.heading: Sharing news about someone you like
A2-24.note: Tina has memorized a person's game schedule and preferences. Her reply about remembering Frank's coffee shows the frankness of close friends.
explanations: “Should” recommends an action.
“Already” emphasizes something completed before now.
“By heart” means memorized well enough to recall easily.

A2-25.scene: At an insurance office. An agent explains a plan to Frank.
A2-25.heading: Checking travel insurance conditions
A2-25.note: A date-of-birth field leads Frank to the date of his creation. His willingness to read long terms creates a characteristically careful joke.
explanations: “Cover” describes what is included in insurance protection.
“Limit” asks for the maximum applicable amount.
“Brought” is the past tense of “bring.”

A2-26.scene: In a café corner, Tina looks pale.
A2-26.heading: Looking for a lost phone
A2-26.note: Hearing her photos are in the cloud, Tina almost looks at the sky. Frank explains Earth's habit of giving one word two meanings.
explanations: The present perfect asks whether a place has already been searched.
“Straight to” means directly, without an intermediate step.
Here, the cloud means internet storage, not clouds in the sky.

A2-27.scene: At an airport baggage counter. Tina asks about her bag.
A2-27.heading: Reporting missing luggage
A2-27.note: The bright pink bag contains an irreplaceable star chart. Discovering that only her luggage went to Paris, Tina answers surprise with humor.
explanations: Explain that luggage failed to appear on the baggage belt.
Use this for an object or place that is very easy to notice.
Describe an unintentional error.

A2-28.scene: At Frank's home. Tina's phone rings while she studies.
A2-28.heading: Passing the phone to a friend
A2-28.note: A quick hello becomes Frank's careful report on Tina's studying and meals. Her mother likes him, extending the invitation to another planet.
explanations: The past continuous describes what was happening before the call.
An informal request to pass the phone to someone.
“Finished” reports a completed task.

A2-29.scene: Frank welcomes Tina at home with tea and homemade cake.
A2-29.heading: Welcoming a friend with tea and cake
A2-29.note: Frank practiced the cake twice for Tina. His modest explanation reveals the care he took preparing for her visit.
explanations: “Try” encourages someone to sample food or drink.
“Smell like” compares a smell with something familiar.
“Again” and a future time invite another visit.

A2-30.scene: At a shop. Tina returns a broken product bought yesterday.
A2-30.heading: Asking for a refund on a broken item
A2-30.note: An attempted repair has left three spare screws. As Tina requests a refund, Frank's part in helping becomes increasingly clear.
explanations: “Full refund” requests all of the purchase price back.
The present perfect checks whether a possible remedy was attempted.
Here, ask whether the dismantled object was put together again.

A2-31.scene: In Tina's room. Frank rushes in holding his phone.
A2-31.heading: Sharing news of a popular video
A2-31.note: The flat voice Tina teases is praised online as calming. Frank is surprised to be accepted just as he looks and sounds.
explanations: “Go viral” means spread rapidly online.
A million is 1,000,000; half a million is 500,000.
Here, “message” is a verb meaning contact by message.

A2-32.scene: Frank phones a restaurant to change a booking.
A2-32.heading: Changing a restaurant reservation
A2-32.note: Frank requests more seats and a table away from desserts. Past experience with Tina informs his careful seating negotiation.
explanations: Describe the reservation you want to change after the noun.
A booking number identifies a specific reservation.
Use “move” to request a change of date.

A2-33.scene: At a café. Tina complains about a roommate.
A2-33.heading: Discussing shared household chores
A2-33.note: Tina's roommate will not wash dishes, so Frank explains his numbering system. Since he lives alone, it cannot quite solve her problem.
explanations: The present perfect asks whether a direct conversation has already been tried.
“Chore” means a routine household task.
“Calm” describes the tone of the proposed conversation.

A2-34.scene: At a new job's induction. A trainer explains the schedule to Frank.
A2-34.heading: Asking about workplace training
A2-34.note: Told he needs no preparation, Frank has already read the manual closely. The new employee's precise questions surprise the trainer.
explanations: “Each day” asks about the daily time required.
“Beforehand” means in advance.
A useful way to begin questions after an explanation.

A2-35.scene: At night in Tina's room. She is absorbed in her phone.
A2-35.heading: Discussing time spent on a phone
A2-35.note: Tina fears missing an important video, though the video features Frank himself. His observation prompts her to reconsider her time.
explanations: The present perfect continuous describes an action continuing over time.
Use “turn off” to stop a function.
“Might” expresses worry about a possibility.

A2-36.scene: At a café. Frank recommends a book he has just finished.
A2-36.heading: Recommending a good book
A2-36.note: Frank even prepares a return agreement before lending a book. He has learned from experience, and Tina responds with a pink pen.
explanations: Show interest and invite someone to continue.
Use “borrow” when you receive something temporarily.
“By” specifies a deadline.

A2-37.scene: At the library counter. Frank has come to pay an overdue fee.
A2-37.heading: Paying a library overdue fee
A2-37.note: For Frank, a simple fee becomes a record of a first failure. Even his reason for keeping the receipt shows his meticulous nature.
explanations: “Overdue” describes a return or payment past its deadline.
“Once” introduces a condition met after something is done.
“May I have” requests something politely.

A2-38.scene: The next morning in Tina's room. She slumps on the sofa.
A2-38.heading: Talking about last night and how you feel
A2-38.note: Tina cannot remember how many drinks she had. Frank notes their differences, then prepares breakfast and sits beside her.
explanations: “Pounding” describes a strong, throbbing feeling.
Say this when you can no longer track a number.
“Gonna” is an informal form of “going to,” used here between close friends.

A2-39.scene: At a bicycle repair shop. A mechanic explains the work to Frank.
A2-39.heading: Arranging bicycle repairs
A2-39.note: Frank even records how often a single bolt loosens. The surprised mechanic understands his wish to ride without falling.
explanations: Ask about a repair or other cost before agreeing.
“Also” adds another request.
“When” specifies the point at which you want a call.

A2-40.scene: At a café. Frank tells Tina about an awkward moment.
A2-40.heading: Talking about an embarrassing event
A2-40.note: Frank was caught passing a note in class. What sounds embarrassing turns out to be a mathematical joke everyone enjoyed.
explanations: “Awkward” describes an uncomfortable situation.
“Catch + person + -ing” means find someone in the middle of an action.
This means spoken audibly rather than read silently.

A2-41.scene: At a pharmacy. Frank collects a new prescription, with Tina accompanying him.
A2-41.heading: Checking how to take medicine
A2-41.note: Tina hears the medicine's effect as magic. Frank checks practical instructions and keeps trying to separate medicine from magic.
explanations: “Twice” gives the count; “a day” means per day.
Check the timing in relation to food.
“Take” is the verb used for consuming medicine.

A2-42.scene: At a café. Tina's deadline is tomorrow; she is on her third coffee.
A2-42.heading: Talking about deadline worries
A2-42.note: Tina wants more coffee; Frank suggests another break. The joke comes when the regular coffee drinker asks her not to copy him.
explanations: “Fall asleep” describes the change from awake to sleeping.
“Nervous about” identifies the cause of anxiety.
Combine “finish” with a specific task and a time.

A2-43.scene: In Tina's room. Her new router will not connect, so she phones a technician. Frank is there too.
A2-43.heading: Discussing an internet connection error
A2-43.note: Frank respects strict rules but dislikes the simple temporary password. Tina celebrates being online while he continues the debate.
explanations: “Plug into” means connect to a power socket or similar connection.
Ask someone to read an on-screen message aloud.
Politely ask someone to wait while you check or work.

A2-44.scene: At a café. Tina reports on competition with a gym friend.
A2-44.heading: Comparing progress in exercise
A2-44.note: Told consistency matters, Tina promises to keep going until she wins. She thinks stopping after victory was included in the promise all along.
explanations: A comparative describes differences in the rate of improvement.
“Skip” means miss a planned activity.
“More” and “less” contrast changes in quantity.

A2-45.scene: At a donation center. Tina brings two bags of old clothes, with Frank accompanying her.
A2-45.heading: Donating clothes with memories
A2-45.note: Tina passes on the coat that once warmed them as students. Rather than losing a memory, she entrusts it with warming someone new.
explanations: “In need” describes people who need assistance.
“Separately” means apart from other things.
Here, “let go” means stop keeping a possession.

A2-46.scene: In Tina's room. Another disappointing online order has arrived, and Frank takes a look.
A2-46.heading: Talking about clothes bought online
A2-46.note: The jacket is too large for Tina but perfect for Frank. Just as the problem seems solved, she reveals that she bought three.
explanations: “Different from” introduces the thing being compared.
“Fit” describes clothing being the right size.
“On sale” means sold at a reduced price.

A2-47.scene: At a veterinary clinic. Tina brings a friend's dog she is looking after; Frank accompanies her.
A2-47.heading: Explaining an animal's condition
A2-47.note: The dog refusing dog food has eaten plenty of treats. As the menu is revealed, the question of who trained whom is reversed.
explanations: “Since” identifies the start of a continuing situation.
“Anything else” checks another possibility.
“Piece” counts a portion of food or another object.

A2-48.scene: Leaving a cinema after an emotional film.
A2-48.heading: Sharing thoughts about a moving film
A2-48.note: Frank insists he did not cry, but Tina's short prompt breaks his defense. Enjoy the contrast between a big reaction and a small admission.
explanations: Introduce something you are a little reluctant to admit.
“Find one's way” means reach a destination by finding a route.
Add this before or after sharing your real feelings.

A2-49.scene: At work. Frank asks his manager for next Friday off.
A2-49.heading: Requesting time off at work
A2-49.note: The manager mistakes a day with Frank's best friend for a date. Frank handles a project deadline while continuing to correct the misunderstanding.
explanations: “Take a day off” means have a day's leave.
“Before” specifies a time earlier than the stated point.
“By” sets the latest acceptable time.

A2-50.scene: In Tina's room. She shows Frank the planet tattoo added inside her left wrist yesterday.
A2-50.heading: Showing a new tattoo
A2-50.note: Tina wears her home planet on her skin. As Frank questions her claim of bravery, he discovers someone else's courage instead.
explanations: The planet image lets her feel that home stays close.
Use “hurt” to ask whether something was painful.
Use a number with “times” to count occurrences.

A2-51.scene: At a language school's reception. Tina applies on a tablet, with Frank accompanying her.
A2-51.heading: Signing up for a language course
A2-51.note: Wanting better conversation skills, Tina checks fees and documents in order. Her familiar birthplace becomes a new case for the receptionist.
explanations: “Fill out” means complete the fields in a form.
“Which” and “should” ask for advice about a choice.
“Documents” are papers needed for a procedure.

A2-52.scene: At a café. Tina's friend Sarah has canceled at the last minute again.
A2-52.heading: Asking about a last-minute cancellation
A2-52.note: Frank considers her friend's circumstances but encourages Tina to explain her hurt feelings too. The source of his convincing advice emerges at the end.
explanations: Describe something happening just before an arranged event.
“Space” can mean emotional room or distance from others.
“How you feel” expresses your feelings.

A2-53.scene: At a phone shop. Frank discusses plans while Tina waits beside him.
A2-53.heading: Checking a mobile phone plan
A2-53.note: Hearing about lower costs, Tina jumps to the conclusion that Frank's number will change. Her panic reveals that she knows it by heart.
explanations: “Save” asks about spending that can be avoided.
“Stay the same” describes remaining unchanged.
The present simple can ask about a fixed start date.

A2-54.scene: In the classroom. Tina slips in late again.
A2-54.heading: Explaining why you are late
A2-54.note: Instead of leaving earlier, Tina proposes being told an earlier class time. Frank's reply finds a flaw in that strategy too.
explanations: Use “for” to describe how long you waited.
Follow “because of” with a noun giving the cause.
“Earlier” compares the time with a previous one.

A2-55.scene: At a police station. Tina's bag was snatched while she walked alone; she called Frank to help report it.
A2-55.heading: Describing an incident and lost belongings
A2-55.note: The bright bag with her name written large now provides a useful clue. Frank reconsiders his opinion of Tina's conspicuous tastes.
explanations: Ask where an event occurred.
“Look like” asks about appearance.
Use this to retract something you previously said.

A2-56.scene: At a clinic. Frank has stomach pain; a worried Tina accompanies him.
A2-56.heading: Explaining the course of symptoms
A2-56.note: Tina is so worried she answers before Frank can. His relief concerns both the pain and the doctor's instruction that he rest quietly at night.
explanations: The present perfect asks how long a symptom has continued.
“Get worse” describes a deterioration.
A short expression when a worry is removed.

A2-57.scene: Tina has finished the term's last exam. A two-week break is approaching.
A2-57.heading: Making plans after exams
A2-57.note: Frank even schedules rest. As Tina anticipates free time, he measures the available fun in minutes.
explanations: “Finally” emphasizes a long-awaited completion.
“Lately” often describes a recent situation with the present perfect.
Use “last” as a verb to ask about duration.

A2-58.scene: At the gym. Tina discusses new goals with a trainer.
A2-58.heading: Discussing new gym goals
A2-58.note: Tina becomes interested in core strength when it promises better photos. Asked for daily changes, she ends by changing her pose.
explanations: “Aim for” introduces a goal.
Use “or” to compare two options when asking advice.
“Stick with” means continue rather than give up.

A2-59.scene: At a station. Bad weather has delayed trains, and Tina has an important meeting.
A2-59.heading: Asking about a train delay
A2-59.note: Tina has reported a major disaster to work, but a taxi might still get her there. The dramatic message creates a different awkwardness.
explanations: “Due to” gives a cause and is common in announcements.
Use “delay” to ask how late a service is.
Recommend keeping a message brief and clear.

A2-60.scene: The end of the year, at Frank's home.
A2-60.heading: Expressing thanks for the year
A2-60.note: Frank nearly leaves Tina off a list because she has helped every day. His careful accounting becomes a way to express straightforward gratitude.
explanations: Use “thank” as a verb followed by the recipient.
A short way to share someone's feeling or experience.
“To” introduces the subject of a toast or wish.
